results.claim: Definition 3.7 (log-average of lambda(a_1 n+b_1)...lambda(a_k n+b_k)/n = o(log omega)) holds for every fixed k and every fixed admissible affine data; attributed to arXiv:1708.02610 plus arXiv:1710.02112, with the all-orders case to arXiv:1809.02518.
results.paper_quote: 1708.02610 Thm 1.1(i): 'For any even k>=0 (which corresponds to an odd number of shifts), and any integers h_0,...,h_k (not necessarily distinct), the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture (3) holds.' Eq (8) gives the affine forms lambda(q_0 n+h_0)...lambda(q_k n+h_k) only 'if k is even'. 1809.02518: 'the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture has been established for k=2 in [29] and for all odd values of k in [32]' (even k>=4 open).
results.doc_quote: THEOREM 3.9 (log-averaged Chowla for all orders — Tao–Teräväinen). Definition 3.7 holds for every fixed `k` and every fixed admissible affine data.
results.notes: Read v2 HTML + abs of 1708.02610, and abs + HTML of 1809.02518. The paper's abstract claims only 'the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture for odd order correlations'; no numbered 'all orders' result exists. 1710.02112 is the odd-order paper, so it cannot supply even k either. The archive's own file tpp-dict-03-almost-all-scales.md quotes 1809.02518 as covering 'k odd or equal to 2' only, contradicting this file's 'every fixed k'.

results.claim: For 1-bounded multiplicative g_0,...,g_k the correlation sequence a -> lim (1/log w_m) sum_{x_m/w_m<=n<=x_m} g_0(n+ah_0)...g_k(n+ah_k)/n is a uniform limit of periodic sequences; if g_0...g_k does not weakly pretend to be a Dirichlet character it vanishes identically, and the periodic approximants are chi-isotypic otherwise.
results.paper_quote: 1708.02610 Thm 1.2 (v2; Thm 1.1 in v1/Duke): '(i) f is the uniform limit of periodic functions f_i. (ii) If the product g_0...g_k does not weakly pretend to be chi for any Dirichlet character chi, then f vanishes identically. (iii) If instead ... weakly pretends to be a Dirichlet character chi, then the periodic functions f_i from part (i) can be chosen to be chi-isotypic in the sense that one has the identity f_i(ab)=f_i(a)chi(b) ...'. Abstract: 'these sequences f are the uniform limit of periodic sequences f_i' and 'then f must vanish identically'.
results.doc_quote: THEOREM 3.13 (the structure theorem for correlations; the modern "why"). For 1-bounded multiplicative g_0, …, g_k, the correlation sequence a ↦ lim (1/log ω_m) Σ_{x_m/ω_m ≤ n ≤ x_m} g_0(n+ah_0)⋯g_k(n+ah_k)/n is a uniform limit of periodic sequences; if g_0⋯g_k does not weakly pretend to be a Dirichlet character, it vanishes identically and the periodic approximants are χ-isotypic otherwise.
results.notes: Faithful to the paper's Thm 1.2 (v2) = Thm 1.1 (v1/Duke); numbering differs from both, so the archive's 'THEOREM 3.13' is an internal label, not the paper's. Display matches the paper's (7) except the paper's outer operator is a generalised limit 'lim~' (archive drops the tilde; the paper invites assuming limits converge). Hypothesis 1<=omega_m<=x_m appears only in the archive's hypotheses list. The paper never asserts lambda weakly pretends to be nothing (that is standard L-function input, the archive's own gloss), and 1809.02518 gives only an almost-all-scales (log-log-in-d, generalised-limit) analogue, not a pointwise unweighted structure theorem.
